summary: GLM-5.2's ModelOpt FP4 metadata leaves shared experts unquantized while routed experts are packed NVFP4. The GLM DSA fusion gate accepted this mixed layout, causing the reported fused-slot shape mismatch. The gate now disables fusion only for that precision mismatch and preserves fusion for uniformly quantized checkpoints.

tests.what_was_measured: The exact GLM-5.2 architecture and ModelOpt exclusion pattern returned no disable reason before the fix; the independent uniform-FP4 boundary passed.
Four GLM fusion-gate cases passed, including mixed ModelOpt FP4 rejection, uniform ModelOpt FP4 preservation, W4AFP8 rejection, and DSA architecture identity.
Three neighboring GLM ModelOpt tests and two subtests passed, including mixed versus uniform shared-expert quantization boundaries.
Changed Python sources compile and the patch has no whitespace errors.
35 tests passed; one unrelated existing assertion assumes EP fusion is blocked off ROCm, but the prepared gfx950 ROCm environment legitimately permits it.

gpu_evidence: Inventory only: one AMD Instinct MI350X, capability (9, 5), PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. No GPU kernel was needed for the loader decision regression, and this is not the reported SM120 hardware.
remaining_limitations: The original eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 TP=8 launch was not run because neither SM120 hardware nor GLM-5.2-NVFP4 weights are available.
This patch addresses the 3072-versus-6144 weight-load mismatch only; SM120 DSA execution depends on separate FlashInfer/DeepGEMM architecture support identified in the issue history.
Ruff is not installed in the prepared interpreter; py_compile and git diff --check were used for static validation.
